author: Linnaeus, 1758
habitat: 해안의 간척지, 염전, 소택지, 하구, 모래가 섞인 갯벌
summary: 봄과 가을에 아주 적은 수가 서해안과 남동 해안을 지나가는 나그네새다. 해안의 간척지, 염전, 소택지, 하구 등에 들르며, 특히 모래가 섞인 갯벌을 좋아한다. 갯지렁이와 작은 새우 같은 바다 무척추동물을 주로 잡아먹는다. 동북 시베리아 북극권과 알래스카에 분포하며, 번식지에서는 한배에 알 4개를 낳는다.

art.subject: Spoon-billed Sandpiper (Calidris pygmaea), adult in breeding plumage, as seen on Korean west-coast tidal flats in May: face, throat, neck and upper breast bright rufous-orange; crown rufous with fine dark streaks; mantle and scapulars with black centres and rufous to buff fringes; lower edge of the rufous breast and the breast sides marked with small dark spots; rest of the underparts white. Bill black, narrowing behind the tip and then broadening into a flat, round-ended spatula; dark eye; black legs.
art.pose: feeding on a sandy mudflat, probing with its spoon-shaped bill
art.scene: Korean west-coast sandy tidal flat near a river mouth in May, wet sand and shallow pools at low tide; no people, buildings or text
views: adult breeding (May), side view standing: rufous-orange face, throat and upper breast, small dark spots along the lower breast border, black-centred rufous-fringed upperparts, white belly, black spatulate bill, black legs

adult non-breeding (late autumn), side view standing: pale grey-brown upperparts with dark shaft streaks, white forehead and broad white supercilium, white breast with a little grey on the sides, black bill and legs
head detail, seen from the front and slightly above: black bill narrowing behind the tip and broadening into a flat, rounded spoon at the end
art.build: Small, stocky stint, about 15cm, the size of a Red-necked Stint and a little larger than a tree sparrow; large head, short neck, horizontal stance. Bill black, about as long as the head, widening only in its outer third into a flat spoon; from the side the tip looks merely deepened, and the spoon shape is clear from the front or from above. Legs black and short. Feeds with a side-to-side sweeping motion of the bill in wet mud and shallow water. In flight a narrow white wing-bar and white sides to a dark rump.
avoid: Do not paint an oversized spoon like a spoonbill or shoveler; the spatula is small and sits at the very tip of a stint-sized bill.
Do not paint a fine pointed bill tip; that is Red-necked Stint (Calidris ruficollis), which otherwise looks very similar.
Do not paint pale or yellowish legs.
Do not paint the rufous breeding face on the non-breeding bird.
